2608.21074.title: PromptResponse: Optimizing Prompts for LLM Coding Tasks
2608.21074.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in research workflows and software development pipelines, yet their output remains sensitive to input prompt variations. This paper presents $\unicode{x00AB}$PromptResponse$\unicode{x00BB}$, a controlled study examining how formatting and LLM-based tuning of coding task prompts affect the resulting code's performance, efficiency, and stability. Using five semantically identical yet syntactically distinct variants of the HumanEval dataset$\unicode{x2014}$baseline, JSON, Markdown, YAML, and an LLM-tuned version$\unicode{x2014}$we had GPT-4o solve its coding problems over 8200$\unicode{x00A0}$executions. Our results show that consistent formatting$\unicode{x2014}$especially JSON$\unicode{x2014}$improves generation efficiency and syntactic stability, with minor gains in task performance. Conversely, the LLM-tuned prompts resulted in significantly degraded task performance without significant improvements in any other dimension. These findings suggest that low-effort reformatting alone can yield measurable improvements, while tuning must account for model alignment. We conclude our work with providing a set of practical recommendations informed by our results as well as releasing our dataset variants and evaluation pipeline for future work.
2608.21074.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在研究工作流程和軟體開發管道中的使用越來越普遍，但它們的輸出仍然對輸入提示的變化敏感。本文提出了「PromptResponse」，這是一項控制研究，檢視格式化和基於LLM的編碼任務提示調整如何影響生成代碼的性能、效率和穩定性。使用五種語義上相同但語法上不同的HumanEval數據集變體——基準、JSON、Markdown、YAML，以及一個經過LLM調整的版本——我們讓GPT-4o在8200次執行中解決其編碼問題。我們的結果顯示，一致的格式化——特別是JSON——改善了生成效率和語法穩定性，對任務性能的提升則較小。相反，LLM調整的提示導致任務性能顯著下降，而在其他維度上並未有顯著改善。這些發現表明，僅進行低成本的重新格式化就能帶來可測量的改善，而調整必須考慮模型的對齊。我們的工作以提供一系列基於我們結果的實用建議作結，並釋出我們的數據集變體和評估管道以供未來的研究使用。
